chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who intends the Hajj: can he remove (his hair) from his head during all of Shawwal, as long as he has not seen the crescent? He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem, as long as he has not seen the crescent.

key_terms.الْهِلَال: The crescent moon, used to determine the start of Islamic months
key_terms.شَوَّال: Shawwal, the tenth month of the Islamic lunar calendar
key_terms.يَأْخُذُ: To take/remove (referring to cutting or shaving hair)

ai.seo_question: When can a pilgrim trim their hair before Hajj if the crescent hasn't been seen?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of a pilgrim trimming their hair during Shawwal, contingent upon the non-sighting of the Dhu al-Qadah crescent, highlighting the reliance on lunar visibility in Shia jurisprudence. It underscores the practical flexibility granted to pilgrims to prepare for Hajj before entering the state of Ihram, reflecting the dynamic nature of Islamic calendar calculations. The ruling emphasizes that the prohibition on cutting hair begins only upon the confirmation of the sacred month, not merely its arrival.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al A’ala who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who intends the Hajj, can he take off (his hair) from his head during Shawwal, all of it, for as long as he does not see the crescent (of Zilqadah)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem for as long as he does not see the crescent’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Husayn ibn abu al-‘Ala’ who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who wants to go for al-Hajj, if he can shave all of his head before seeing the new moon.
He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful before seeing the new moon. ‘“
